knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Definite Integral of a Rational Function Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =5 x^{4} + 4 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =20 x^{3} \\ \text{d}u & =20 x^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}u & =x^{3}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=5 x^{4} + 4.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 1 \\ u & 4 & 9\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\int_{0}^{1}\frac{10 x^{3}}{5 x^{4} + 4}\,\text{d}x=\int_{4}^{9}\frac{10}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{4}^{9}\frac{10}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{20}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{2}\int_{4}^{9}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\ln(u)|_{4}^{9} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\ln(9)-\ln(4)) \\  & =- \log{\left(2 \right)} + \log{\left(3 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: a*x^n+b>0 throughout closed original x interval; no poles
